products.name: asset_sampling_point
products.description: This association product represents the operational configuration between physical infrastructure assets and water quality sampling points. It captures the many-to-many relationship where a single asset (e.g., storage tank, pump station) can have multiple designated sampling locations (inlet, outlet, overflow, different depths), and a single sampling point can monitor water quality across multiple interconnected assets (e.g., a distribution system sampling point representing multiple mains). Each record defines the sampling configuration, frequency overrides, priority ranking, and access logistics specific to each asset-sampling point pair.. Existence Justification: In water utility operations, the relationship between physical assets and sampling points is genuinely many-to-many. A single asset such as a storage tank has multiple designated sampling locations (inlet, outlet, overflow, different depths for stratification monitoring), and a single sampling point in the distribution system can monitor water quality across multiple interconnected assets (mains, valves, service connections). The utility actively manages these sampling configurations as part of regulatory compliance and operational monitoring programs, with each asset-sampling point pair having specific frequency overrides, priority rankings, and access logistics. products.name: grant_funding
products.description: This association product represents the funding relationship between physical infrastructure assets and grants. It captures the allocation of grant funds to specific assets, tracking the funding amount, percentage, compliance status, and funding period for each asset-grant combination. Each record links one asset to one grant with attributes that exist only in the context of this funding relationship, supporting audit trails, reimbursement tracking, and grantor compliance reporting.. Existence Justification: In water utility capital finance, individual infrastructure assets (treatment plant upgrades, main replacements, pump stations) are routinely funded through multiple concurrent grants (DWSRF, CWSRF, EPA WIFIA, state programs, ARPA), and each grant program funds multiple assets across capital improvement projects. The utility must track the specific funding amount, percentage, compliance status, and reimbursement details for each asset-grant combination to support grantor reporting, single audit requirements (SEFA schedules), and drawdown requests.

products.name: compliance_requirement
products.description: This association product represents the compliance relationship between physical infrastructure assets and regulatory requirements. It captures the specific compliance obligations, assessment schedules, and compliance status for each asset-requirement pair. Each record links one asset to one regulatory requirement with attributes that track compliance method, assessment dates, variance status, and compliance state specific to that asset-requirement combination.. Existence Justification: In water utility operations, a single physical asset (e.g., a chlorine contact basin) must comply with multiple overlapping regulatory requirements from different regulatory programs (SDWA Surface Water Treatment Rule for CT requirements, state disinfection rules, EPA DBP rules for chlorine residual limits, NPDES for discharge). Conversely, a single regulatory requirement (e.g., SDWA Lead and Copper Rule) applies to multiple different asset types across the utility (service lines, treatment plant corrosion control systems, distribution system storage tanks, sampling stations). The compliance relationship itself carries operational data including compliance status, assessment schedules, compliance methods, and variance status that are specific to each asset-requirement pair.

products.name: analytical_result
products.description: Laboratory and field analytical result for each parameter tested on a collected water sample or measured by a continuous online instrument. Captures analyte/contaminant reference, CAS number, analytical method (EPA method number), result value, unit of measure, detection limit (MDL/MRL), qualifier flags (non-detect, estimated, hold-time exceeded, presence/absence), result type (grab, composite, continuous, calculated), measurement source (laboratory, field, SCADA/online), laboratory accreditation number, analyst ID, analysis date/time, QA/QC batch reference, instrument ID for online readings, and monitoring period context. Supports all parameter types including conventional chemistry, DBP species, PFAS compounds, bacteriological presence/absence, turbidity NTU, chlorine residuals, and CT calculations. Links to water_sample for discrete samples and online_instrument for continuous readings. Sourced from LIMS (LabWare) and OSIsoft PI Historian. Note: Individual PFAS compound results are stored here for lab-level detail; pfas_monitoring provides the regulatory compliance context, hazard index calculations, and treatment trigger evaluations that aggregate across compounds.

attributes.name: applicable_regulation
attributes.description: Citation of the regulation or rule establishing this limit. Examples: '40 CFR 141.80' (Stage 2 DBPR), '40 CFR 141.51' (MCLs for inorganic contaminants), 'LCRR 40 CFR 141.80-141.91', state-specific regulation citation, or facility NPDES permit number.

attributes.name: averaging_period
attributes.description: Time period over which the limit is calculated or averaged. Instantaneous = single sample, daily_max = maximum value in a day, monthly_avg = average over calendar month, quarterly_avg = average over quarter, annual_avg = average over calendar year, running_annual_avg = rolling 12-month average, locational_running_annual_avg = running annual average at specific sampling location (e.g., for DBPs under Stage 2 DBPR). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: instantaneous|daily_max|monthly_avg|quarterly_avg|annual_avg|running_annual_avg|locational_running_annual_avg — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]. Ref: Sensus AMI.

attributes.description: Indicates whether this contaminant must be included in the annual Consumer Confidence Report (CCR) distributed to drinking water customers. True = must report in CCR, False = not required in CCR. Ref: Sensus AMI.

attributes.name: contaminant_limit_code
attributes.description: The contaminant limit code value recorded for each contaminant limit in the quality domain.

attributes.name: compliance_status
attributes.description: Current status of this limit record. Active = currently enforceable, superseded = replaced by newer limit, pending = future effective date not yet reached, suspended = temporarily not enforced due to variance or waiver. Ref: Sensus AMI.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this contaminant limit record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking. Ref: Sensus AMI.

attributes.name: contaminant_limit_description
attributes.description: The contaminant limit description value recorded for each contaminant limit in the quality domain.

attributes.name: detection_limit_required
attributes.description: Minimum detection limit (MDL) or practical quantitation limit (PQL) required for the analytical method. Laboratory results must meet or exceed this sensitivity. Expressed in same unit_of_measure as limit_value. Ref: Sensus AMI.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date when this contaminant limit became or will become enforceable. Critical for compliance tracking and historical analysis. Ref: Sensus AMI.

attributes.name: exceedance_action_required
attributes.description: Description of required actions when this limit is exceeded. Examples: 'Public notification within 24 hours', 'Implement corrosion control treatment', 'Increase monitoring frequency', 'Submit corrective action plan within 30 days', 'Immediate discharge cessation'. Ref: Sensus AMI.

attributes.name: health_effect_category
attributes.description: Primary health effect category associated with this contaminant. Acute = immediate health impact, chronic = long-term exposure health impact, carcinogen = cancer-causing, developmental = impacts fetal/child development, reproductive = impacts reproductive health, aesthetic = non-health impact (taste, odor, color). Ref: Sensus AMI.

attributes.name: jurisdiction
attributes.description: Regulatory jurisdiction imposing this limit. Federal = EPA national standard, state = state primacy agency standard (may be more stringent than federal), local = municipal or county requirement, permit_specific = facility-specific limit in NPDES or discharge permit. Ref: Sensus AMI.

attributes.name: jurisdiction_authority
attributes.description: Name of the regulatory authority or agency that issued this limit. Examples: 'U.S. EPA', 'California State Water Resources Control Board', 'Ohio EPA', 'Local Municipal Authority', or specific permit-issuing agency. Ref: Sensus AMI.

attributes.name: limit_type
attributes.description: Type of regulatory or operational limit. MCL = Maximum Contaminant Level (enforceable), MCLG = Maximum Contaminant Level Goal (non-enforceable health goal), action_level = threshold triggering corrective action (e.g., Lead and Copper Rule), treatment_technique = required treatment process standard, permit_limit = facility-specific NPDES or discharge permit limit. Ref: Sensus AMI.

attributes.name: limit_value
attributes.description: Numeric threshold value for the contaminant limit. For example, MCL for lead is 0.015 mg/L. Null if limit is qualitative (e.g., treatment technique with no numeric threshold). Ref: Sensus AMI.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The modified timestamp associated with each contaminant limit record in the quality domain.

attributes.name: monitoring_frequency_required
attributes.description: Required sampling and analysis frequency for this contaminant at this context. Examples: 'Quarterly', 'Monthly', 'Weekly', 'Daily', 'Continuous', 'Every 3 years', 'Per compliance schedule'. May reference a compliance_schedule record for complex schedules. Ref: Sensus AMI.

attributes.name: contaminant_limit_name
attributes.description: The contaminant limit name used to identify each contaminant limit record in the quality domain.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Additional context, clarifications, or special conditions related to this contaminant limit. May include information about seasonal variations, conditional applicability, calculation methods, or references to related compliance obligations. Ref: Sensus AMI.

attributes.name: public_notification_tier
attributes.description: Public notification tier required when this limit is violated (drinking water only). Tier_1 = immediate notice (within 24 hours) for acute health risk, tier_2 = notice within 30 days for chronic health risk, tier_3 = notice within 1 year for monitoring/reporting violations, not_applicable = no public notification required (e.g., for wastewater limits). Ref: Sensus AMI.

attributes.name: sample_location_type
attributes.description: Type of location where samples are collected for comparison against this limit. Entry_point = water entering distribution system, distribution_system = within distribution network, consumer_tap = at customer premise, source_water = raw water intake, effluent_discharge = treated wastewater discharge point, process_intermediate = within treatment process.

attributes.name: contaminant_limit_status
attributes.description: The contaminant limit status value recorded for each contaminant limit in the quality domain.

attributes.name: superseded_date

attributes.name: unit_of_measure
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the limit value. attributes.name: updated_timestamp

attributes.name: variance_expiration_date

attributes.name: variance_waiver_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a variance or waiver has been granted for this limit at this monitoring context. True = variance/waiver in effect (limit may be temporarily relaxed or monitoring reduced), False = standard limit applies without exception. Ref: Sensus AMI.

products.name: exceedance
products.description: Transactional record of each confirmed MCL, action level, or permit limit exceedance detected from analytical results. Captures exceedance date, contaminant, sampling point, measured value, applicable limit, exceedance magnitude, regulatory notification deadline, public notification requirement flag, corrective action required, and resolution status. This is the primary operational record driving regulatory response workflows and violation tracking.

products.name: dbp_monitoring_event
products.description: Specialized transactional record for Disinfection Byproduct (DBP) monitoring events under Stage 2 DBPR rules. Captures monitoring period, LRAA (Locational Running Annual Average) calculation inputs, THM and HAA5 individual species results (chloroform, bromodichloromethane, dibromochloromethane, bromoform; monochloroacetic acid, dichloroacetic acid, trichloroacetic acid, monobromoacetic acid, dibromoacetic acid), TTHM and HAA5 totals, compliance status, and system-wide running annual average. products.name: pfas_monitoring
products.description: Tracks individual PFAS compound monitoring results including PFOA, PFOS, PFNA, PFHxS, PFBS, and HFPO-DA (GenX). Calculates hazard index for PFNA+PFHxS+PFBS+HFPO-DA per EPA PFAS NPDWR. Records MCL compliance status, monitoring period, sampling point, treatment response triggers, and supports both US EPA SDWA PFAS regulations and EU Drinking Water Directive 2020/2184 sum-of-20 and total PFAS limits. Links to water samples, analytical results, and treatment technology responses (GAC, ion exchange, RO). Supports UCMR5 reporting and state-specific PFAS monitoring requirements.

products.name: turbidity_reading
products.description: High-frequency turbidity monitoring records from continuous online instruments and grab samples at WTP filter effluents, combined filter effluent, and distribution entry points. Captures NTU value, measurement timestamp, instrument ID, measurement method (nephelometric), filter unit number, CT compliance context, IFE (Individual Filter Effluent) vs CFE (Combined Filter Effluent) designation, and exceedance flag against Surface Water Treatment Rule turbidity limits. Sourced from OSIsoft PI Historian via SCADA integration.

products.name: ct_calculation
products.description: Disinfection CT (Contact Time) calculation records for each WTP disinfection process. Captures calculation date/time, disinfectant type (chlorine, chloramine, ozone, UV), disinfectant residual concentration (C in mg/L), contact time (T in minutes), calculated CT value (mg·min/L), required CT for 3-log Giardia and 4-log virus inactivation, CT ratio (achieved/required), temperature, pH, and compliance status. Sourced from OSIsoft PI Historian. Critical for Surface Water Treatment Rule compliance.

attributes.name: population_served_count

attributes.name: preparation_start_date

attributes.name: primacy_agency

attributes.name: publication_date

attributes.name: published_flag

attributes.name: regulatory_body_name

attributes.name: regulatory_directive_reference

attributes.name: report_status

attributes.name: report_year

attributes.name: reporting_year

attributes.name: source_water_assessment_summary
attributes.description: Summary of the source water assessment including susceptibility to contamination and availability information. Required CCR content element. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: special_notices_included
attributes.description: Description of any special notices included in the CCR such as boil water advisories, vulnerable population warnings, or emerging contaminant information.

attributes.name: ccr_period_status
attributes.description: The ccr period status value recorded for each ccr period in the quality domain.

attributes.name: treatment_technique_violation_count
attributes.description: Number of treatment technique violations that occurred during the report year. Treatment techniques are required processes for contaminants without MCLs. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: violation_summary

attributes.name: water_source_summary

attributes.name: created_by

attributes.name: ccr_modified_by_user_employee_id

attributes.name: primary_ccr_employee_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the water quality manager or compliance officer who reviewed and approved this contaminant detection record for inclusion in the Consumer Confidence Report. Supports audit trail and regulatory accountability. Ref: Sensus AMI.

attributes.name: quality_sampling_point_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to quality.sampling_point. Business justification: CCR detected contaminants are detected at specific sampling points. This FK identifies the primary sampling point where the contaminant was detected, enabling location-specific reporting in the CCR. Ref: Sensus AMI.

attributes.name: segment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to customer.customer_segment. attributes.name: tertiary_ccr_modified_by_user_employee_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the user who last modified this contaminant detection record. Supports change tracking and accountability for data quality. Ref: Sensus AMI.

attributes.name: water_system_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the water system referenced by each ccr detected contaminant record in the quality domain.

attributes.name: action_level
attributes.description: The concentration of a contaminant which, if exceeded, triggers treatment or other requirements that a water system must follow. Primarily used for lead and copper under the Lead and Copper Rule (LCR) and Lead and Copper Rule Revisions (LCRR). Null if not applicable.

attributes.name: approval_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this contaminant detection record was reviewed and approved for CCR publication. Part of the quality assurance and regulatory compliance workflow. Ref: Sensus AMI.

attributes.name: ccr_table_display_order
attributes.business_glossary_term: Consumer Confidence Report (CCR) Table Display Order
attributes.description: Sequence number controlling the display order of this contaminant in the published CCR detected contaminants table. Allows utilities to organize contaminants by category, regulatory importance, or alphabetically for public presentation. Ref: Sensus AMI.

attributes.name: ccr_detected_contaminant_code
attributes.description: The ccr detected contaminant code value recorded for each ccr detected contaminant in the quality domain.

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Internal notes, comments, or observations regarding this contaminant detection. May include quality control notes, data validation comments, or context for unusual results. Not published in the CCR but retained for internal documentation. Ref: Sensus AMI.

attributes.name: compliance_status
attributes.description: Overall compliance status for this contaminant during the reporting period. Indicates whether the water system met all regulatory requirements including MCL/AL compliance, monitoring frequency, and reporting obligations. Ref: Sensus AMI.

attributes.name: contaminant_category
attributes.description: Classification of the contaminant type for regulatory grouping and CCR presentation. Categories align with EPA National Primary Drinking Water Regulations structure. Ref: Sensus AMI.

attributes.name: corrective_action_description
attributes.description: Description of corrective actions taken or planned by the water system in response to violations or elevated contaminant levels. Required disclosure in CCR when violations occur. Includes treatment modifications, infrastructure improvements, or operational changes. Ref: Sensus AMI.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this contaminant detection record was first created in the system. Part of the audit trail for regulatory compliance and data governance. Ref: Sensus AMI.

attributes.name: data_source
attributes.description: Identifies the system or process from which this contaminant detection data was obtained (e.g., Laboratory Information Management System, SCADA historian, manual data entry, state drinking water database). Supports data lineage and quality assurance. Ref: Sensus AMI.

attributes.name: ccr_detected_contaminant_description
attributes.description: The ccr detected contaminant description value recorded for each ccr detected contaminant in the quality domain.

attributes.name: detected_level
attributes.description: The detected level value recorded for each ccr detected contaminant in the quality domain.

attributes.name: detection_frequency_percent
attributes.description: Percentage of samples in which this contaminant was detected, calculated as (number_of_detections / number_of_samples) * 100. Provides statistical context for contaminant presence in the water system. Ref: Sensus AMI.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The effective date associated with each ccr detected contaminant record in the quality domain.

attributes.name: footnote_text
attributes.description: Additional explanatory text or footnotes specific to this contaminant detection that will appear in the CCR. Used to provide context, explain unusual results, clarify monitoring schedules, or reference specific regulatory requirements. Ref: Sensus AMI.

attributes.name: health_effects_language
attributes.description: EPA-mandated health effects language describing the potential health impacts of this contaminant when present above the MCL or MCLG. Must use EPA-approved standard language as specified in 40 CFR 141.153 Appendix B. Required for all contaminants with violations or detections above health-based levels. Ref: Sensus AMI.

attributes.name: highest_level_detected
attributes.description: The highest single measurement or calculated running annual average (RAA) of the contaminant detected during the reporting period. For some contaminants (e.g., THM, HAA5), this represents the highest locational running annual average (LRAA). Reporting format depends on contaminant-specific regulations. Ref: Sensus AMI.

attributes.name: mcl
attributes.description: The Maximum Contaminant Level (MCL) - the highest level of a contaminant that is allowed in drinking water. MCLs are enforceable standards set as close to MCLGs as feasible using the best available treatment technology. Null if a Treatment Technique (TT) applies instead of an MCL. Ref: Sensus AMI.

attributes.name: mcl_value
attributes.description: The mcl value value recorded for each ccr detected contaminant in the quality domain.

attributes.name: mclg
attributes.description: The Maximum Contaminant Level Goal (MCLG) - the level of a contaminant in drinking water below which there is no known or expected risk to health. MCLGs are non-enforceable public health goals. Value of zero indicates no safe level. Null indicates no MCLG established. Ref: Sensus AMI.

attributes.name: mclg_value
attributes.description: The mclg value value recorded for each ccr detected contaminant in the quality domain.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this contaminant detection record was last modified. Supports change tracking and audit requirements for regulatory reporting. Ref: Sensus AMI.

attributes.name: monitoring_period_end_date
attributes.description: The ending date of the monitoring period for which this contaminant detection data was collected. Defines the temporal scope of the reported results. Ref: Sensus AMI.

attributes.name: monitoring_period_start_date
attributes.description: The beginning date of the monitoring period for which this contaminant detection data was collected. Defines the temporal scope of the reported results. Ref: Sensus AMI.

attributes.name: ccr_detected_contaminant_name
attributes.description: The ccr detected contaminant name used to identify each ccr detected contaminant record in the quality domain.

attributes.name: number_of_detections
attributes.description: Count of samples in which this contaminant was detected above the method detection limit (MDL) or practical quantitation level (PQL) during the reporting period. Provides transparency on detection frequency. Ref: Sensus AMI.

attributes.name: number_of_samples
attributes.description: Total count of samples collected and analyzed for this contaminant during the reporting period. Used to demonstrate compliance with monitoring frequency requirements and provide context for detection statistics. Ref: Sensus AMI.

attributes.name: public_notification_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this contaminant detection triggered Public Notification (PN) requirements under 40 CFR 141 Subpart Q. True if Tier 1, 2, or 3 public notice was required, False otherwise. Public notification is separate from but related to CCR reporting. Ref: Sensus AMI.

attributes.name: range_high
attributes.description: The highest level detected for this contaminant across all samples collected during the reporting period. Forms the upper bound of the detection range required for CCR reporting. Typically matches highest_level_detected unless different averaging methods apply. Ref: Sensus AMI.

attributes.name: range_low
attributes.description: The lowest level detected for this contaminant across all samples collected during the reporting period. Forms the lower bound of the detection range required for CCR reporting. May be zero or below detection limit. Ref: Sensus AMI.

attributes.name: regulatory_program
attributes.description: The specific EPA regulatory program or rule under which this contaminant is monitored and reported (e.g., National Primary Drinking Water Regulations, Lead and Copper Rule, Disinfectants and Disinfection Byproducts Rule, Unregulated Contaminant Monitoring Rule). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: npdwr|surface_water_treatment_rule|groundwater_rule|lead_copper_rule|dbp_rule|radionuclides_rule|unregulated_contaminant_monitoring — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: reporting_year
attributes.description: Calendar year for which this contaminant detection is being reported in the CCR. Typically the year in which samples were collected and analyzed. Ref: Sensus AMI.

attributes.name: sample_year
attributes.description: The actual year in which the water samples were collected for this contaminant. May differ from reporting year for contaminants with multi-year monitoring cycles (e.g., lead and copper, certain synthetic organic chemicals). Ref: Sensus AMI.

attributes.name: ccr_detected_contaminant_status
attributes.description: The ccr detected contaminant status value recorded for each ccr detected contaminant in the quality domain.

attributes.name: treatment_technique_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this contaminant is regulated by a Treatment Technique (TT) requirement rather than an MCL. True if TT applies (e.g., turbidity, lead and copper action levels), False if MCL applies. Ref: Sensus AMI.

attributes.name: typical_source_description
attributes.description: EPA-mandated language describing the likely sources of this contaminant in drinking water. Must use EPA-approved standard language for each contaminant as specified in 40 CFR 141.153 Appendix A. This text appears directly in the published CCR. Ref: Sensus AMI.

attributes.name: unit_of_measure
attributes.description: The unit of measurement for contaminant concentration values (e.g., mg/L for milligrams per liter, ug/L for micrograms per liter, pCi/L for picocuries per liter, NTU for Nephelometric Turbidity Units, MFL for million fibers per liter). Must align with EPA reporting standards. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: mg/L|ug/L|pCi/L|MFL|NTU|%|CFU/100mL|MPN/100mL — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]. Ref: Sensus AMI.

attributes.name: violation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the detected contaminant level resulted in a violation of the MCL, MCLG, Treatment Technique, or Action Level during the reporting period. True if violation occurred, False if compliant. Violations must be prominently disclosed in the CCR. Ref: Sensus AMI.

attributes.name: violation_type
attributes.description: Classification of the type of violation if violation_flag is True. Specifies whether the violation was due to MCL exceedance, action level exceedance, treatment technique failure, monitoring failure, or reporting failure. Value is 'none' if no violation occurred. Ref: Sensus AMI.

products.name: monitoring_waiver
products.description: Master record of approved monitoring waivers granted by the primacy agency allowing reduced monitoring frequency for specific contaminants at specific sampling points. Captures waiver type (vulnerability assessment, source water, contaminant-specific), contaminant group, waiver approval date, expiration date, reduced monitoring frequency, primacy agency approval reference, and conditions for waiver continuation. Ensures the sampling_schedule correctly reflects waiver-adjusted requirements.

attributes.name: water_system_id

attributes.name: approval_date

attributes.name: ccr_reporting_impact

attributes.name: monitoring_waiver_code

attributes.name: created_timestamp

attributes.name: monitoring_waiver_description
attributes.description: The monitoring waiver description value recorded for each monitoring waiver in the quality domain.

attributes.name: effective_date

attributes.name: expiration_date

attributes.name: historical_monitoring_period_end

attributes.name: historical_monitoring_period_start
attributes.description: Start date of the historical monitoring period used to demonstrate non-detect results for waiver eligibility. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: modified_by

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this monitoring waiver record was last modified or updated in the system. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: monitoring_waiver_name
attributes.description: The monitoring waiver name used to identify each monitoring waiver record in the quality domain.

attributes.name: next_renewal_date
attributes.description: Date by which the waiver renewal application must be submitted or the waiver reassessment must be completed. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: primacy_agency_approval_reference

attributes.name: primacy_agency_name
attributes.description: Name of the state or federal primacy agency that approved and granted the monitoring waiver (e.g., State Department of Environmental Quality, EPA Region). Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: reduced_monitoring_frequency
attributes.description: Reduced monitoring frequency allowed under the waiver (e.g., annual, triennial, once per compliance period). Expressed as a frequency code or description. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: renewal_frequency_years
attributes.description: Frequency in years at which the waiver must be renewed or reassessed if renewal is required. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: renewal_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the waiver requires periodic renewal or reapplication (True) or is granted indefinitely subject to conditions (False). Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: responsible_department
attributes.description: Department or organizational unit responsible for waiver compliance and monitoring (e.g., Water Quality, Regulatory Compliance, Laboratory). Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: revocation_date
attributes.description: Date on which the waiver was revoked by the primacy agency or voluntarily withdrawn by the utility, if applicable. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: revocation_reason
attributes.description: Detailed explanation of the reason for waiver revocation, including regulatory violations, detection events, or operational changes. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: revocation_trigger_conditions
attributes.description: Specific conditions or events that would trigger automatic revocation of the waiver (e.g., detection above action level, source water contamination, operational changes). Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: sampling_schedule_adjustment_notes
attributes.description: Operational notes describing how the sampling schedule must be adjusted to reflect the waiver-reduced monitoring frequency. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: monitoring_waiver_status
attributes.description: The monitoring waiver status value recorded for each monitoring waiver in the quality domain.

attributes.name: vulnerability_assessment_date
attributes.description: Date on which the vulnerability assessment or source water assessment supporting the waiver was completed. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: vulnerability_assessment_result
attributes.description: Outcome of the vulnerability assessment indicating the level of vulnerability to the contaminant at the sampling point (e.g., not vulnerable, low vulnerability). Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: waiver_conditions
attributes.description: Specific conditions, requirements, or restrictions imposed by the primacy agency for maintaining the waiver (e.g., annual source water monitoring, notification requirements, operational changes). Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: waiver_duration_years
attributes.description: Duration of the monitoring waiver in years, representing the period between effective date and expiration date. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: waiver_justification
attributes.description: Detailed business and regulatory justification for granting the monitoring waiver, including vulnerability assessment results, historical non-detect data, or source water protection measures. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: waiver_number
attributes.description: Externally-known unique identifier or reference number assigned by the primacy agency or utility for this monitoring waiver. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: waiver_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the monitoring waiver indicating whether it is active, expired, revoked, pending approval, suspended, or renewed. Ref: EPA SDWA.

attributes.name: waiver_type

products.name: online_instrument
products.description: Master registry of continuous online water quality monitoring instruments deployed across WTPs, WWTPs, and the distribution network. Captures instrument type (turbidimeter, chlorine analyzer, pH meter, TOC analyzer, UV254 sensor, flow meter), manufacturer, model, serial number, installation location/sampling point, calibration frequency, last calibration date, calibration standard used, communication protocol (SCADA/Modbus/HART), PI Historian tag name, and operational status. Distinct from the asset domain's general asset registry by focusing on quality-specific instrument metadata and calibration management.

products.name: territory_contaminant_monitoring_requirement
products.description: This association product represents the territory-specific monitoring requirements and regulatory variances between contaminants and service territories. It captures jurisdiction-specific monitoring frequencies, action levels, and variance statuses that exist only in the context of a specific contaminant being monitored within a specific service territory. Each record links one contaminant to one service territory with regulatory override attributes that reflect primacy agency decisions, vulnerability assessments, and approved variances.. Existence Justification: In water utility operations, contaminants have different monitoring requirements across service territories based on primacy agency jurisdiction, source water vulnerability assessments, and approved regulatory variances. A single contaminant (e.g., lead) may require quarterly monitoring in one territory but have a waiver for reduced frequency in another territory based on vulnerability assessment results. Conversely, a single service territory must track territory-specific monitoring requirements, action levels, and variance statuses for dozens of regulated contaminants. This is an operational compliance management relationship that utilities actively maintain.

attributes.name: collection_equipment_code

attributes.name: collection_equipment_description

attributes.name: collection_latitude

attributes.name: collection_location_name

attributes.name: collection_longitude

attributes.name: collection_method_code
attributes.description: Standardized code identifying the sample collection method used (e.g., grab sample, composite sample, continuous monitoring). Must align with EPA-approved methods. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: collection_method_description
attributes.description: Detailed description of the collection method, including any deviations from standard protocols or special handling requirements. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: collection_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for documenting any unusual conditions, deviations from standard procedures, or observations made during sample collection. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: collection_status

attributes.name: collection_timestamp

attributes.name: collector_certification_number
attributes.description: Certification or license number of the sample collector, demonstrating qualification to perform regulated sample collection activities. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: collector_name

attributes.name: compliance_monitoring_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this sample is part of regulatory compliance monitoring (true) or operational/investigative monitoring (false). Compliance samples have stricter QA/QC and reporting requirements. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: composite_duration_hours
attributes.description: For composite samples, the total time period over which the sample was collected in hours (e.g., 24-hour composite). Null for grab samples. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: composite_interval_minutes
attributes.description: For composite samples, the time interval between individual aliquot collections in minutes. Null for grab samples. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: container_type
attributes.description: Type of sample container used (e.g., glass bottle, plastic bottle, sterile bag). Must be appropriate for the analytes being tested and comply with EPA protocols. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this collection event record was first created in the LIMS or data management system. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: field_conductivity_us_cm

attributes.name: field_dissolved_oxygen_mg_l
attributes.description: Dissolved oxygen concentration measured at the time of collection in mg/L. Important for wastewater treatment process control and environmental discharge monitoring. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: field_ph
attributes.description: pH level measured at the time of collection. Indicates acidity or alkalinity of the water sample. Required field measurement for many regulatory programs. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: field_residual_chlorine_mg_l
attributes.description: Free or total chlorine residual measured at the time of collection in mg/L. Critical disinfection parameter for drinking water distribution system monitoring. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: field_temperature_c
attributes.description: Water temperature measured at the time of collection in degrees Celsius. Critical field parameter for sample integrity and regulatory compliance. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: field_turbidity_ntu
attributes.description: Turbidity measured at the time of collection in NTU. Key indicator of water clarity and treatment effectiveness, with strict regulatory limits for drinking water. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: flow_rate_gpm
attributes.description: Flow rate at the sampling point at the time of collection in gallons per minute. Used for flow-weighted composite calculations and process monitoring. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: modified_by
attributes.description: User ID or name of the person who last modified this collection event record. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this collection event record was last modified. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: mvm_tier
attributes.description: The mvm tier value recorded for each sample collection event in the laboratory domain.

attributes.name: preservative_used

attributes.name: regulatory_program

attributes.name: sample_matrix
attributes.description: The physical medium or matrix of the sample collected (drinking water, raw water, wastewater, effluent, sludge, biosolids). Determines applicable analytical methods and regulatory thresholds. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: sample_type
attributes.description: Classification of the sample based on collection approach: grab (single point in time), composite (time or flow-weighted), continuous, or QA/QC samples (duplicate, blank, spike). Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: sample_volume_ml
attributes.description: Total volume of the sample collected in milliliters. Must meet minimum volume requirements for planned analytical tests. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: vibe_added_flag
attributes.description: The vibe added flag value recorded for each sample collection event in the laboratory domain.

attributes.name: weather_conditions
attributes.description: Description of weather conditions at the time of sample collection (e.g., clear, rain, snow, fog). Relevant for source water and stormwater sampling events. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: created_by
attributes.description: User ID or name of the person who created this collection event record in the system. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

products.name: chain_of_custody
products.description: Legal and regulatory chain of custody record tracking the possession, transfer, and handling of samples from collection through final disposition. Records each custody transfer (collector to courier, courier to lab, lab to archive), transfer datetime, condition of samples at transfer, seal integrity, and signatures of transferring and receiving parties. Required for EPA-defensible data and NPDES/SDWA compliance.
products.reference: Cited standards & systems of record: LabWare LIMS; ISO/IEC 17025

attributes.name: chain_of_custody_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the chain of custody record. Primary key for tracking legal and regulatory custody transfers from sample collection through final disposition. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: cip_project_id
attributes.description: Reference to the monitoring project or compliance program associated with this sample. Used for cost allocation and regulatory reporting. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: collected_by_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Chain of custody regulatory compliance requires documented employee accountability for sample collection. EPA and state regulations mandate traceable custody records with employee identification for l. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: customer_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to customer.customer_account. attributes.description: Foreign key linking to laboratory.sample_collection_event. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: sampling_location_id
attributes.description: Reference to the geographic location where the sample was collected. Links to GIS (Geographic Information System) location master. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: collection_datetime

attributes.name: collector_certification_number

attributes.name: collector_signature

attributes.name: container_count

attributes.name: corrective_action_taken

attributes.name: courier_tracking_number
attributes.description: Tracking number provided by courier service for shipment traceability. Used to verify delivery and resolve custody disputes. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: created_timestamp

attributes.name: custody_document_number
attributes.description: Externally-known unique document number for the chain of custody form. Used for legal traceability and audit purposes. Format: COC-YYYYMMDD-XXXXXX. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: custody_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the chain of custody record. Tracks progression from sample collection through final disposition. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: discrepancy_description
attributes.description: Detailed description of any discrepancies noted during custody transfer. Required for corrective action and regulatory reporting. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: discrepancy_noted
attributes.description: Indicates whether any discrepancies were noted during the custody transfer (e.g., missing samples, damaged containers, documentation errors). Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: hold_time_compliant
attributes.description: Indicates whether the sample was received within the maximum allowable hold time specified by the analytical method. Non-compliance may invalidate results. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: ice_present
attributes.description: Indicates whether ice or cooling packs were present in the sample cooler at the time of receipt. Required for temperature-sensitive samples. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: modified_by
attributes.description: Username or identifier of the person who last modified this chain of custody record. Audit trail field for data governance. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this chain of custody record was last modified in the LIMS (Laboratory Information Management System). Audit trail field. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: mvm_tier
attributes.description: The mvm tier value recorded for each chain of custody in the laboratory domain.

attributes.name: preservation_method
attributes.description: Chemical or physical preservation method applied to the sample (e.g., HCl, H2SO4, refrigeration, none). Must match method requirements. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: preservation_verified
attributes.description: Indicates whether the sample preservation was verified at receipt (e.g., pH check for acid preservation). Required for regulatory compliance. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: received_by
attributes.description: Full name of the person receiving custody of the sample during this transfer event. Part of the legal custody chain. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: received_datetime
attributes.description: Date and time when custody was received by the receiving party. Critical for establishing unbroken custody chain and hold time compliance. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: received_signature
attributes.description: Digital or scanned signature of the person receiving custody. Required for legal chain of custody documentation. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: relinquished_by
attributes.description: Full name of the person relinquishing custody of the sample during this transfer event. Part of the legal custody chain. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: relinquished_datetime
attributes.description: Date and time when custody was relinquished by the transferring party. Critical for establishing unbroken custody chain. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: relinquished_signature
attributes.description: Digital or scanned signature of the person relinquishing custody. Required for legal chain of custody documentation. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: remarks
attributes.description: Additional notes or comments regarding the custody transfer, sample condition, or special handling requirements. Free-text field for documentation. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: sample_condition_at_transfer
attributes.description: Observed physical condition of the sample at the time of custody transfer. Critical for determining sample integrity and data usability. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: seal_intact
attributes.description: Indicates whether the custody seal on the sample container or cooler was intact at the time of transfer. Critical for establishing sample integrity. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: seal_number
attributes.description: Unique identifier of the tamper-evident seal applied to the sample container or cooler. Used to verify custody integrity. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: temperature_at_receipt_c
attributes.description: Measured temperature of the sample or cooler at the time of receipt. Must be within acceptable range (typically 0-6°C) for regulatory compliance. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: temperature_compliant
attributes.description: Indicates whether the sample temperature at receipt was within the acceptable range specified by the analytical method. Non-compliance may invalidate results. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: transfer_type
attributes.description: Classification of the custody transfer event. Identifies the stage in the sample lifecycle where custody changed hands. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: vibe_added_flag
attributes.description: The vibe added flag value recorded for each chain of custody in the laboratory domain.

attributes.description: Unique identifier for the analytical test record. Primary key for the analytical test entity. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: analyte_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific chemical, physical, or biological parameter being measured (e.g., lead, total coliform, pH, turbidity, PFAS). Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: calibration_curve_id
attributes.description: Reference to the instrument calibration curve used to convert raw instrument response to analyte concentration. Links to calibration standards, curve coefficients, and correlation coefficient (R²). Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: cip_project_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to project.cip_project. Business justification: Analytical tests are frequently performed for specific capital projects (new treatment plant startup, pipeline disinfection verification, construction phase monitoring). Required for project cost allo. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Individual test costs must be allocated to the requesting department's cost center for interdepartmental billing and budget tracking. Water utilities operate labs as internal service centers that char. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: lab_instrument_id
attributes.description: Reference to the laboratory instrument or equipment used to perform the test (e.g., ICP-MS, spectrophotometer, incubator). Links to calibration and maintenance records. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: lab_sample_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent laboratory sample on which this analytical test was performed. Links to the sample collection and chain of custody record. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: primary_analytical_certified_analyst_id
attributes.description: Reference to the certified laboratory analyst who performed the test. Used for quality assurance, proficiency tracking, and regulatory audit trails. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: qc_batch_id
attributes.description: Reference to the quality control batch that includes this test. QC batches contain blanks, duplicates, spikes, and control standards to validate analytical accuracy and precision. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: tertiary_analytical_approved_by_analyst_certified_analyst_id
attributes.description: Reference to the laboratory director or authorized signatory who provided final approval for the test result. Approved results are certified for regulatory reporting and external release. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: test_method_id
attributes.description: Reference to the standardized analytical test method applied (e.g., EPA 200.7, SM 2540C, ASTM D1067). Defines the procedure, detection limits, and quality control requirements. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: accreditation_body
attributes.description: Name of the organization that accredited the laboratory to perform this test method (e.g., NELAC, A2LA, ANAB, state primacy agency). Required for regulatory acceptance of results. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: accreditation_number
attributes.description: Unique certificate or license number issued by the accreditation body authorizing the laboratory to perform this test method. Must be current and valid for regulatory reporting. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: approval_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the test result received final approval and was certified for regulatory reporting. Marks transition to approved status and enables result release. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: chain_of_custody_number
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the chain of custody document that accompanied the sample from collection through laboratory receipt. Ensures sample integrity and traceability for legal defensibility. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this analytical test record was first created in the laboratory system. Represents the initial entry into the laboratory workflow. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: detection_limit
attributes.description: Minimum concentration of analyte that can be measured and reported with 99% confidence that the value is greater than zero. Used to determine non-detect results and reporting limits. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: dilution_factor
attributes.description: Multiplier applied to raw instrument response to account for sample dilution performed to bring analyte concentration within instrument calibration range. A value of 1.0 indicates no dilution. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: hold_time_compliant_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the test was performed within the maximum allowable time between sample collection and analysis. Hold times vary by analyte and method (e.g., 48 hours for bacteria, 28 days for metals). Non-compliance may invalidate results for regulatory reporting. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this analytical test record was most recently updated. Tracks changes to results, status transitions, or corrections throughout the test lifecycle. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: lims_import_timestamp
attributes.business_glossary_term: Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) Import Timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this test record was imported from the source Laboratory Information Management System (LabWare) into the enterprise data lakehouse. Used for data lineage and reconciliation. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

tag_set.value: Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) Import Timestamp

attributes.name: matrix_type
attributes.description: Classification of the sample medium being analyzed. Matrix type affects method selection, quality control requirements, and regulatory applicability. Different matrices may require different preparation techniques and have different interference profiles. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: drinking_water|raw_water|wastewater|groundwater|surface_water|biosolids|soil|sediment — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: mvm_tier
attributes.description: The mvm tier value recorded for each analytical test in the laboratory domain.

attributes.name: percent_recovery
attributes.description: Quality control metric indicating the percentage of known analyte concentration recovered in matrix spike or laboratory control sample. Used to assess method accuracy and matrix interference. Acceptable ranges are method-specific. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: preservation_method
attributes.description: Chemical or physical treatment applied to the sample to maintain analyte stability during storage and transport (e.g., acidification with HNO3, refrigeration at 4°C, addition of sodium thiosulfate for dechlorination). Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: qualifier_code
attributes.description: Data quality flag indicating special conditions affecting the result. U=non-detect (below detection limit), J=estimated value (between MDL and RL), B=blank contamination detected, E=exceeds calibration range, H=hold time exceeded, N=tentative identification, Q=QC failure, R=rejected, S=spike recovery out of range, T=temperature exceedance, V=value verified, X=other (see comments). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: U|J|B|E|H|N|Q|R|S|T|V|X — 12 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: raw_instrument_response
attributes.description: Uncorrected measurement value directly from the analytical instrument before applying dilution factors, calibration curves, or other corrections. Retained for audit trails and method validation. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: reanalysis_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the test must be repeated due to quality control failure, questionable results, or regulatory requirements. Triggers workflow to schedule reanalysis from the same sample or request new sample collection. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: regulatory_program
attributes.description: Federal or state regulatory program under which this test is being performed. Determines applicable compliance thresholds, reporting requirements, and data quality objectives. SDWA=Safe Drinking Water Act, CWA=Clean Water Act, NPDES=National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: sdwa|cwa|npdes|rcra|cercla|tsca|state_program — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: rejection_reason
attributes.description: Detailed explanation for why the test result was rejected and cannot be used for regulatory reporting. Common reasons include QC failure, hold time exceedance, contamination, instrument malfunction, or analyst error. Triggers resampling or reanalysis. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: relative_percent_difference
attributes.description: Quality control metric measuring precision between duplicate samples. Calculated as the absolute difference divided by the mean, expressed as a percentage. Used to assess analytical reproducibility. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: reporting_limit
attributes.description: Minimum concentration that can be reliably quantified and reported. Typically set at 2-10 times the Method Detection Limit (MDL) to ensure data quality and regulatory compliance. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: result_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the result value (e.g., mg/L, ug/L, NTU, MPN/100mL, pH units, CFU/100mL). Must align with regulatory reporting requirements and Maximum Contaminant Level (MCL) units. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: result_value
attributes.description: Calculated analytical result value after applying dilution factors, calibration curves, and method-specific calculations. This is the reportable concentration or measurement for the analyte. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: review_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the test result was reviewed and validated by a senior analyst or supervisor. Marks transition from preliminary to reviewed status.

attributes.name: test_comments
attributes.description: Free-text field for analyst notes, observations, or explanations regarding unusual conditions, deviations from standard procedures, or result interpretation. May include details on matrix interference, instrument issues, or quality control anomalies. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: test_completion_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the analytical test procedure was completed and raw results were recorded. Used to calculate turnaround time and verify hold time compliance. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: test_number
attributes.description: Human-readable business identifier for the analytical test, often used in laboratory worksheets, chain of custody forms, and external reporting. May follow lab-specific numbering conventions. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: test_priority
attributes.description: Business priority classification for the analytical test. STAT tests require immediate processing for operational decisions; regulatory tests support compliance reporting deadlines; routine tests follow standard turnaround times. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: test_start_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the analytical test procedure was initiated. Critical for hold time compliance and contact time (CT) calculations for disinfection validation. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: test_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the analytical test. Tracks progression from initiation through final approval or rejection. Preliminary results are unvalidated; reviewed results have passed QC checks; approved results are certified for regulatory reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: pending|in_progress|preliminary|reviewed|approved|rejected|cancelled — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: uncertainty_value
attributes.description: Quantified estimate of the doubt associated with the measurement result, expressed in the same units as the result. Includes contributions from sampling, sample preparation, calibration, and instrument variability. Ref: LabWare LIMS.

attributes.name: vibe_added_flag
attributes.description: The vibe added flag value recorded for each analytical test in the laboratory domain.

products.name: test_result
products.description: Validated and finalized analytical result record produced from an analytical test. Stores the reported result value, reporting unit, detection status (detected, non-detect, trace), result qualifier, uncertainty estimate, approved result flag, approving analyst, approval datetime, and the regulatory parameter it maps to (e.g., MCL, MCLG, NPDES effluent limit). Distinct from analytical_test which captures the raw in-process measurement; test_result is the authoritative reported value released for compliance and operational use.
